stem.en: Kabir asks why the messenger "does not just go inside and switch on the phosphorylase itself". What does the relay buy?

text.en: Amplification and a chance to control. One molecule outside becomes millions of switched enzymes inside, which a single molecule wandering in could never do. And every step of the chain is a place where the cell can turn the message up, down or off.
Nothing; it would be simpler inside.

feedback.en: One molecule inside could switch on one enzyme. The cell needs a million switched on in seconds.

text.en: The messenger is too big to enter.

feedback.en: Some messengers are small enough and still stay outside, because the relay is the point.

text.en: The wall would leak if messengers came through.

feedback.en: Nothing is punched. The receptor passes the shape change through the wall with no hole at all.

explanation.en: A relay is a series of wheels. Each turns many. The message grows at every step and can be adjusted at every step.
